observed_behavior: Invalid id-less batch members produce validation errors.
This package treats explicit null as a request and replies with id null; the peer treats it as a notification and returns HTTP 204.
Both preserve 9007199254740993 without binary floating-point loss; this package correlates 1, 1.0, and 1e0 by exact numeric value while the peer exposes them as distinct lexical IDs.
The peer returns parse error while this package returns the normative Invalid Request object.
Every invalid member contributes an Invalid Request response.
Both implementations currently preserve response order without making it portable.
Malformed JSON and invalid envelopes retain distinct error codes.
Ambiguous duplicate members are rejected instead of selecting a value.
Both implementations return HTTP 204 with an empty body for notification-only requests.
Both require POST and use HTTP 200 for JSON-RPC errors; this package additionally accepts application/json-rpc and application/*+json while the peer returns HTTP 415.
